title: Fixed finite basis for rational representations
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], with $k$ and $V$ in one fixed universe $u$. Put $n=\dim_k V$. Define the finite index set $I(V)=\operatorname{ULift}_u(\operatorname{Fin}(n))$, and fix the $k$-basis $b_V$ of $V$ indexed by $I(V)$ obtained from the standard chosen finite basis $\operatorname{finBasis}_k(V)$ indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ by reindexing along the inverse of the lift equivalence. Thus $b_V(\operatorname{up}(j))=\operatorname{finBasis}_k(V)(j)$. The zero space is allowed, in which case $I(V)$ and the basis are empty. This is the fixed basis convention for identifying $\mathrm{GL}(V)$ with a matrix general linear group.
